title: Queue Fallback Orchestration and Soft Throttling for Multi-Region Stability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional overload or downstream degradation we currently either outright reject requests or apply blunt global caps that harm high-priority customers. We need a finer-grained, multi-region aware mechanism that gracefully reduces resource consumption while preserving latency SLOs for critical traffic and avoiding global cascading failures.

Goal: Implement a queue orchestration layer that coordinates per-region ephemeral queues, performs soft throttling (delay + lightweight degradations) and orchestrates controlled failover to remote regions or cheaper model variants when necessary. The system should be policy-driven, observable, and reversible by runbook or automated SLO triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Canary deploy in eu-west-1 handling 10% of traffic: soft-throttle paths exercised with no more than 5% increase in p50 and preserving p99 latency SLO for tier-1 tenants
Grace levels implemented: DELAY (client-visible short delay), TRUNCATE (return partial/summary output), REDIRECT (route to secondary region/model), REJECT (final fallback)
Per-route policy config UI + API in console and feature-flag toggle for experiments
Dashboards show queue occupancy, average soft-throttle delay, degrade-mode hit-rate, and error-budget burn per-region
Automated rollback if error rate increases >200% above baseline or if 10m sustained p99 breach
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer temporary, reversible soft degradations over immediate hard rejects to maintain developer UX and avoid automated client retries that amplify load.
We will avoid tenant-wide hard caps. Instead use dynamic per-route prioritization with a simple priority mapping (tier-1,tier-2,tier-3) supplied by auth token metadata.
Soft throttling actions ordered by cost-impact: 1) small randomized delay (50-500ms), 2) compress/summary output, 3) shorten max_tokens, 4) route to cheaper quantized model / secondary region.
Latency SLOs targeted: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms for tier-1 within region; soft-throttle should preserve these for tier-1 under mild overload.
Will implement a policy evaluator library in runtime that is lightweight and suitable for hot path execution; policies stored in control plane with aggressive caching.
Circuit-breaker integration: the orchestrator will watch regional health and decide to escalate degradations or initiate cross-region reroute when capacity fallbacks occur.
Avoiding cascading failure: introduce backoff windows and minimum dwell time before lowering degradation level to prevent flip-flop.

Security: no customer data modification in degrade modes; summaries must be deterministic and respect PII redaction policies. Security review not required for core orchestration (operator controls only).
comments: 2026-02-20 Asha Patel: Initial scoping completed. Spiked two approaches: a) centralized coordinator with per-region agents, b) fully decentralized agents with shared policy. Leaning toward hybrid to reduce control plane latency.

2026-02-26 Diego Martinez: Prototype of soft-delay middleware running in runtime agent. Observed 30% reduction in peak CPU when delaying 100-200ms for low-priority requests. Need to validate client retry behavior.
2026-03-02 Priya Singh (SRE): Added SLO guardrails for automated escalation. Recommend circuit breaker threshold of 20% capacity loss sustained for 30s before cross-region failover.
2026-03-05 Product review (Liam Chen): PMs requested explicit rate for degrade-mode hits exposed in Console and per-customer opt-outs for summary responses.
2026-03-08 Diego Martinez: Integration tests passing in staging. Created PR with runtime changes and policy API (see links). Kicked off a canary plan for week of 2026-03-15.
2026-03-10 Asha Patel: Risk review: potential increased egress cost for cross-region redirects. Finance asked for budgeting guardrails; added 'max-cross-region-routes' per-tenant policy.
2026-03-10 SRE on-call (Oliver Reed): Runbook draft uploaded; includes steps to force degrade-levels and how to interpret degrade-mode metrics.
risk: Cross-region reroute may increase latency for some traffic; must be communicated to customers via status fields
Misconfigured policies could unintentionally degrade high-value customers; require deploy-time validation and canary rollout
Egress costs could rise if reroute thresholds are lax; finance threshold guard added
